definitions.meaning: One unbroken loop of components joined by wires, around which charge flows; break the loop anywhere and the flow stops everywhere.
The flow of charge around the loop, measured in amps by an ammeter; in a series loop it is the same at every point.
The agreed direction of current flow: out of the battery's positive terminal, around the loop, and back into the negative terminal.
An arrangement with only one path for the charge, so every component carries the same current and one break stops everything.
An arrangement where each component sits on its own branch, so one can fail while the others keep working.
How much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms; in Ohm's law, V = I R, a fixed 4 ohm resistance lets 12 volts drive 3 amps.
The relation V = I R between voltage, current and resistance: with resistance fixed, doubling the voltage doubles the current.
The unit of current: the series loop in the animation carries 0.5 amps, read the same on both sides of the bulb.

mechanismSteps: The loop: battery, bulb and ammeter joined by wires form one unbroken loop - the battery pushes charge around it, the bulb turns electrical energy into light, and the ammeter measures the flow.
Direction: conventional current leaves the positive terminal, crawls around the loop, and returns to the negative terminal - follow the red markers.
Paths: in series there is one path and one broken bulb kills the loop; in parallel each bulb has its own branch, so one can fail and the other stays lit.
Ohm's law: with resistance fixed at 4 ohms, stepping the battery from 6 to 12 volts speeds the markers up and climbs the ammeter from 1.5 to 3 amps - 12 divided by 4 is 3.
Not used up: ammeters before and after the bulb in a series loop both read 0.5 amps - the bulb changes energy's form, not the current's size.
Summary: current flows positive to negative around a single loop, series means one path while parallel means many, and the series current is identical everywhere under V = I R.
objectives: Describe a simple circuit as one unbroken loop and state what the battery, bulb and ammeter each do
State the direction of conventional current and compare series and parallel circuits
Use Ohm's law, V = I R, to calculate current and explain why current is the same everywhere in a series loop
subject: science
title: Electricity: circuits, current and Ohm's law

trap.explanation: The bulb glows and gets hot, so it looks like it consumes the electricity flowing through it. Current is not used up: an ammeter reads the same 0.5 amps on both sides of the bulb. In class, place the ammeter on each side of the bulb in turn: 0.5 A before, 0.5 A after - the bulb changed electrical energy into light and heat, but no current disappeared.
trap.misconception: The bulb uses up the current.

workedExample: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 ohm resistor. Current = voltage / resistance = 12 / 4 = 3 A. Check the units: volts divided by ohms gives amps, and halving the battery to 6 V halves the current to 1.5 A without changing the resistance.
